H6MI02265.name: Charlotta Magoon
H6MI02265.bio: Registered nurse for 17 years in acute care and community health settings in West Michigan.

positions.stance: Supports Medicare for All, a single-payer system covering medical, dental, vision and mental health, and Medicare negotiation of prescription drug prices.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage and workers' right to organize, bargain collectively and strike "without fear of retaliation."
Will fight to protect the Great Lakes, defend clean air standards, invest in renewable energy and stop subsidizing the fossil fuel industry.
Says Congress must set federal zoning guidelines and require environmental review for data centers, and regulate artificial intelligence's rapid expansion.
Supports expanding affordable housing construction, strengthening tenant protections and ending regulations that block new supply.

H6MI02273.name: Richard Sills
H6MI02273.bio: Businessman with experience in print, graphics and marketing and 39 years in livestock and crop production.

positions.stance: Objects to "allocating billions providing free education, free healthcare and infrastructure overseas" while U.S. students, infrastructure and health care struggle.
Says "We have 6 years to fix social security."
Says "the largest financial benefit of the cannabis/hemp plant is in the industrial application," including oil, biodiesel, textiles and construction materials.
Supports vertically integrated domestic production to gain "as much independence from the global energy markets" and oil-based consumer goods as possible.
Supports "fostering good-paying jobs, supporting small business owners, and lowering everyday costs for working families."
Supports "ensuring affordable prescription medications and quality medical care for every family and senior."
Supports "investing in public schools, vocational training, and affordable higher education."
Supports "upgrading roads, bridges, and safeguarding our Great Lakes and local drinking water systems."

H6MI05235.name: Ronald A. Muszynski
H6MI05235.bio: Retired engineer with a Bachelor of Engineering Technology from the University of Toledo; long-time Grass Lake resident.

positions.stance: Says the dollar has lost over 98% of its value since 1971 and calls to "End The Fed," audit the gold reserves and balance the budget.
Opposes "Big Brother surveillance" of phone calls, texts, emails, purchases and travel, noting AI and data centers can now analyze that data quickly.
Says both parties are covering up these crimes with files held in secret, and pledges to "expose and prosecute" those involved.
Opposes "endless wars," saying sending young people to kill another country's children "should be last on a very long list."

H6MI08320.name: C. Mia Pettus
H6MI08320.bio: Former City of Philadelphia police officer and Department of Defense civilian federal police officer; independent researcher and publisher of PALS Report on Substack.

positions.stance: Supports lower grocery prices, lower energy costs, affordable housing and affordable healthcare: "Make Life Affordable Again."
Supports sustainable manufacturing, skilled trades, small business and bringing overseas jobs back: "Build More. Make More. Earn More."
Focuses on public safety, law enforcement, fentanyl, mental health and neighborhood revitalization: "Safe Streets. Strong Communities."
Supports government transparency, oversight, ending waste and whistleblower protections: "Put Taxpayers Before Politicians."
Prioritizes the Fourth Amendment, due process and individual liberty, and calls to "End Surveillance State."

wiki:kwabena-nkromo.name: Kwabena Nkromo
wiki:kwabena-nkromo.bio: Grassroots civic leader, food policy advocate and Green Party organizer with experience in neighborhood organizing, housing justice and community economic development.

positions.stance: Advocates special federal investment to finish replacing remaining water-service infrastructure from municipal systems into affected homes.
Proposes a citizen-led regional economic-revitalization planning process, with federal resources supporting "a locally rooted strategy rather than impose another Washington formula."
Pursues "accessible, affordable, preventive healthcare" and studying high-performing systems, including Massachusetts, to strengthen primary and preventive care.
Supports investing in universities, community colleges, technical education, apprenticeships and affordable higher education for the AI economy.
Supports expanding affordable construction and rehabilitation and backing Community Land Trusts to preserve affordability and community control over land.
Calls to return U.S. soldiers from around the world, talk to all countries, and take a nuclear first strike "off the table."
Supports repealing or radically changing the USA Freedom Act, the Military Commissions Act and FISA, and rejects torture and secret tribunals.
"I believe that there should be no increase in the national debt"; says we must pay our bills as we go.
Seeks a thorough audit of the Federal Reserve and opposes taxpayer bailouts of corporations and corporate subsidies.
Signed the 2022 FAIRtax Pledge supporting H.R. 25, a single-rate federal retail sales tax replacing federal income taxes.

H4MI10131.name: Anil Kumar
H4MI10131.bio: Urologist in private practice for over 30 years, former hospital chief of staff, clinical assistant professor and member of the Wayne State University Board of Governors.

positions.stance: Supports lowering "housing, groceries, healthcare, and everyday costs for working families."
"Healthcare is a right with an affordable public option"; supports lower costs and cheaper prescriptions.
Supports teachers, strengthening public schools, expanding skilled trades and reducing debt.
Supports strengthening Social Security and Medicare and supporting small businesses so "hard work leads to stability."

H6MI11308.name: Ryan Teasdale
H6MI11308.bio: Relationship manager for a community developer whose career has focused on escalated communication and mediation.

positions.stance: Proposes putting all problems on the table and inviting experts and stakeholders from every side to "Collaborative Problem-Solving sessions."
Lists public safety, mental health and emotional proficiency, affordable housing and development, and government and corporate transparency as primary focuses.

H4MI12145.name: Brenda K. Sanders
H4MI12145.bio: Former trial attorney and Michigan judge; author and former radio and podcast host.

positions.stance: Will "immediately bring a resolution and request a vote to restore Medicare Part D Prescription Subsidies in full."
Would sponsor legislation paying $1,000 monthly to families with household income of $65,000 or less, citing job losses from artificial intelligence.
Would sponsor legislation paying reparations to descendants of enslaved people, partly financed by a small tax on New York Stock Exchange transactions.
Would pass a law "declaring Election Day a Federal Holiday."
Opposes abortion and urges voters to "Say no to late term abortion in Michigan."
Says "To end abortion, we too must show the victims," and plans unfiltered TV ads to reach millions of viewers.
Supports "Implementing the Economic Democracy Act" as "A Practical Big solution for a Huge problem."
Supports streamlining the committee and subcommittee structure in Congress.
Supports a single-rate tax system.
Will lead a national discussion focused on "the Whole Person," with "Better communication, proper therapy and less drugs."
Calls to "Bring China before The Hague" over COVID-19 deaths.
